rows: Download a web page and return its Open Graph metadata as a STRUCT, with HTTP status and error.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Fetch each URL over HTTP(S) (following redirects, reading only the document head) and return the same `STRUCT` as parse_opengraph plus final_url (after redirects; relative URLs are resolved against it), http_status `INTEGER`, content_type and error. A page that can't be read does NOT fail the query: its row has error set (e.g. 'HTTP 404 Not Found', 'timed out after 10000 ms', 'not an HTML page …') and NULL metadata, so filter with `WHERE og.error IS NULL`. URLs in one batch are fetched concurrently (8 at a time) and duplicates are fetched once; 429/5xx responses are retried. Tune with the environment variables OPENGRAPH_TIMEOUT_MS, OPENGRAPH_MAX_BYTES, OPENGRAPH_CONCURRENCY and OPENGRAPH_USER_AGENT. Results depend on the live web; if you already have the HTML, use parse_opengraph(html, base_url) instead.

## fetch_opengraph(url)

Download pages and summarize their link-preview metadata. Adds `final_url`, `http_status`, `content_type` and `error` to the `parse_opengraph` fields. Failures are reported in `error` rather than failing the query.

List every <meta> property/name and content pair in an HTML document, in document order.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return a `LIST(STRUCT(property VARCHAR, content VARCHAR))` with every <meta> tag that has a property= or name= attribute and a content= attribute, in document order, duplicates kept. property is lower-cased (og:title, og:image:width, article:published_time, twitter:card, description, …); content is entity-decoded. Use it for properties the parse_opengraph summary doesn't carry (article:*, product:*, og:video:width, multiple og:locale:alternate): unnest the list and filter on t.property. No network access.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## opengraph_tags(html)

Every `<meta property|name=… content=…>` as a list of `{property, content}` structs. `unnest` it to filter, pivot or count properties.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Unnest the raw meta tags of a document","sql":"SELECT t.property, t.content FROM (SELECT unnest(opengraph.main.opengraph_tags('<meta property=\"og:type\" content=\"article\"><meta property=\"article:author\" content=\"Ada\">')) AS t) ORDER BY t.property"},{"description":"Audit where each page's preview title comes from: check the raw tags from opengraph_tags for og:title or twitter:title, else parse_opengraph fell back to the <title> element","sql":"WITH pages(page_url, html) AS (VALUES ('https://shop.example.com/a', '<title>Shop A</title><meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"Spring Sale\">'), ('https://shop.example.com/b', '<title>Shop B</title><meta name=\"twitter:title\" content=\"B on Twitter\">'), ('https://shop.example.com/c', '<title>Shop C</title>')) SELECT page_url, preview_title, CASE WHEN list_contains(props, 'og:title') THEN 'og:title' WHEN list_contains(props, 'twitter:title') THEN 'twitter:title' ELSE '<title> fallback' END AS title_source FROM (SELECT page_url, opengraph.main.parse_opengraph(html).title AS preview_title, [t.property FOR t IN opengraph.main.opengraph_tags(html)] AS props FROM pages) ORDER BY page_url"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description":"Raw meta tags, one row each","sql":"SELECT t.property, t.content FROM (SELECT unnest(opengraph.main.opengraph_tags('<meta property=\"og:type\" content=\"article\"><meta property=\"article:author\" content=\"Ada\">')) AS t) ORDER BY t.property","expected_result":[["article:author","Ada"],["og:type","article"]]}]

WITH pages(page_url, html) AS (VALUES ('https://shop.example.com/a', '<title>Shop A</title><meta property="og:title" content="Spring Sale">'), ('https://shop.example.com/b', '<title>Shop B</title><meta name="twitter:title" content="B on Twitter">'), ('https://shop.example.com/c', '<title>Shop C</title>')) SELECT page_url, preview_title, CASE WHEN list_contains(props, 'og:title') THEN 'og:title' WHEN list_contains(props, 'twitter:title') THEN 'twitter:title' ELSE '<title> fallback' END AS title_source FROM (SELECT page_url, opengraph.main.parse_opengraph(html).title AS preview_title, [t.property FOR t IN opengraph.main.opengraph_tags(html)] AS props FROM pages) ORDER BY page_url
Parse Open Graph, Twitter Card and basic HTML metadata from an HTML document into a `STRUCT`.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Same as parse_opengraph(html) but takes the page's own URL as a second argument and returns every URL-valued field (url, image, images, video, audio, canonical_url, favicon_url, oembed_url) as an absolute URL. Use it when you stored crawled HTML next to its URL: `parse_opengraph(body, page_url)`. A <base href> in the document overrides base_url. Fields: title, description, type, url, site_name, locale, image, image_alt, image_width, image_height, images (list), video, audio, twitter_card, twitter_site, twitter_creator, canonical_url, favicon_url, oembed_url. Fallbacks: title = og:title → twitter:title → <title>; description = og:description → twitter:description → <meta name=description>; url = og:url → <link rel=canonical>; image = first og:image → twitter:image; locale = og:locale → <html lang>. The first occurrence of a property wins. Values are entity-decoded and whitespace-trimmed; absent values are NULL (images is an empty list).
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## parse_opengraph(html, base_url)

Like `parse_opengraph(html)`, with relative URLs resolved against `base_url` (or the page's `<base href>`).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Pull the title and preview image out of an HTML document","sql":"SELECT og.title, og.image FROM (SELECT opengraph.main.parse_opengraph('<html lang=\"en\"><head><title>Fallback</title><meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"Rock & Roll\"><meta property=\"og:image\" content=\"/cover.png\"></head></html>') AS og)"},{"description":"Resolve a relative og:image against the page URL","sql":"SELECT opengraph.main.parse_opengraph('<html lang=\"en\"><head><title>Fallback</title><meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"Rock & Roll\"><meta property=\"og:image\" content=\"/cover.png\"></head></html>', 'https://example.com/music/').image AS image"},{"description":"Build article preview cards from crawled HTML: title and absolute image from parse_opengraph(html, base_url), plus the article:tag keywords (not in the summary) collected from opengraph_tags","sql":"WITH pages(page_url, html) AS (VALUES ('https://blog.example.com/posts/duckdb', '<title>Blog</title><meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"Why DuckDB\"><meta property=\"og:image\" content=\"/img/duck.png\"><meta property=\"article:tag\" content=\"duckdb\"><meta property=\"article:tag\" content=\"sql\">'), ('https://blog.example.com/posts/hello', '<title>Hello, world</title><meta property=\"article:tag\" content=\"intro\">')) SELECT page_url, og.title, og.image, article_tags FROM (SELECT page_url, opengraph.main.parse_opengraph(html, page_url) AS og, [t.content FOR t IN opengraph.main.opengraph_tags(html) IF t.property = 'article:tag'] AS article_tags FROM pages) ORDER BY page_url"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description":"A relative og:image becomes absolute","sql":"SELECT opengraph.main.parse_opengraph('<html lang=\"en\"><head><title>Fallback</title><meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"Rock & Roll\"><meta property=\"og:image\" content=\"/cover.png\"></head></html>', 'https://example.com/music/').image AS image ORDER BY ALL","expected_result":[["https://example.com/cover.png"]]},{"description":"Build article preview cards from crawled HTML: title and absolute image from parse_opengraph(html, base_url), plus the article:tag keywords (not in the summary) collected from opengraph_tags","sql":"WITH pages(page_url, html) AS (VALUES ('https://blog.example.com/posts/duckdb', '<title>Blog</title><meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"Why DuckDB\"><meta property=\"og:image\" content=\"/img/duck.png\"><meta property=\"article:tag\" content=\"duckdb\"><meta property=\"article:tag\" content=\"sql\">'), ('https://blog.example.com/posts/hello', '<title>Hello, world</title><meta property=\"article:tag\" content=\"intro\">')) SELECT page_url, og.title, og.image, article_tags FROM (SELECT page_url, opengraph.main.parse_opengraph(html, page_url) AS og, [t.content FOR t IN opengraph.main.opengraph_tags(html) IF t.property = 'article:tag'] AS article_tags FROM pages) ORDER BY page_url","expected_result":[["https://blog.example.com/posts/duckdb","Why DuckDB","https://blog.example.com/img/duck.png",["duckdb","sql"]],["https://blog.example.com/posts/hello","Hello, world",null,["intro"]]]}]
